tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

If the user specifies an app to use, get the app by name, bundle ID, or path:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Each `cua_repl.js` call opens or continues a browser activity. Keep consecutive calls together. The activity stays open across messages until you emit completion commentary.

**Manual takeover takes priority over the table below.** For a required manual browser step, call the documented takeover API before asking the user to act, unless takeover is already pending. Explain the required step in your final reply. Tab marking alone does not transfer control. While waiting for the user to finish and return control, emit no completion and make no CUA calls, even when answering side questions. The takeover API returning does not end this wait. When the user returns or unblocks you, resume browser work and apply the table. If they cancel, replace, or no longer need the browser work, close the activity before answering, even without another CUA call.

Completion is a standalone assistant commentary message containing only `::browser-complete{title="<headline>"}`. Never put it in a tool call or final reply. Use 3–6 words starting with a past-tense verb to describe the observed outcome. Omit identifiers.

After a user cancels pending browser work: commentary `::browser-complete{title="Stopped browser work"}`, then the final acknowledgement. No browser call is needed.

For an open browser activity:

| Next action                                   | Required output order                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Another CUA call                              | Continue without completion.                                                              |
| A non-CUA tool, final reply, or chat question | Finish required tab marking, emit completion, then take that action in the same response. |

With no open activity, emit no completion. Later CUA use requires a fresh completion at the next table boundary.

If you need a one-time sign-in code, information, or confirmation from the user, follow the table and ask in chat. One-time code entry alone does not require takeover. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.name: js_reset
tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

name: egm-bootstrap
license: Apache-2.0
disable-model-invocation: true
description: Bootstrap directory README.md files across a repository subtree.
---

# EGM Peanuts and Hay Bootstrap (`egm-bootstrap`)

When running in Codex or ChatGPT Work, first read [Codex integration](../../docs/codex.md).
In Claude Code or Cowork, read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/claude.md` first.

Automates creating, updating, and verifying Elephant-and-Goldfish Model (EGM) `README.md` contracts (`Interface`, `Invariants`, `Side Effects`) across a directory tree: **Peanuts** (leaf package contracts) and **Hay** (parent blueprint indexes).

## Inputs

*   **`path`**: Target root directory to bootstrap (Required).
*   **`is_worker`**: Internal; `true` when running as a Sub-Orchestrator (default: `false`).
*   **`sub_tree_root`**: Internal; subtree partition root path.
*   **`target_filename`**: Contract filename to generate or update (default: `"README.md"`, or e.g. `"EGM.md"` when preserving human-written READMEs).

## Execution Constraints (CRITICAL)

1.  **Delegation & Plugin-Root Paths**: Read the *Plugin-Root Resource Paths* and *Subagent Delegation (Goldfish Isolation)* sections of [execution instructions](../../resources/execution_instructions.md) (Claude Code: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/resources/execution_instructions.md`; pathless `<SKILL>`: `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/resources/execution_instructions.md`). Do not apply the `egm-brainstorm`/`egm-draft`/`egm-review` or drafting-only sections here. If file tools cannot read it, apply inline delegation: spawn fresh-context subagents (`invoke_subagent` / `Agent` / `spawn_agent`), use direct dispatch if nesting is unsupported (see [harnesses.md](../../docs/harnesses.md)), or run scout steps inline if no subagent tool exists.
2.  **No Code Generation & VCS Isolation**: Strictly limited to documentation (`README.md` / `target_filename`). Do not write or refactor functional source code, and do not perform version control commits (`git add`, `git commit`). Write all changes locally using standard file-writing tools; tracking and submitting stay with the human user.
3.  **Temporary File Isolation**: Each worker keeps its status, checkpoint, and log files in its own directory outside the workspace (host scratch or `mktemp -d`), never a fixed, shared path. If neither exists, skip them.
4.  **Tool Usage & Formatting**: Use shell and file tools for discovery and contract generation following [README templates](references/templates.md) with clean Markdown (headers, tables, fenced blocks; optionally invoke a configured repo formatter like `npx prettier --write`).
5.  **Subagent Delegation**: Spawn sub-orchestrator workers in parallel (capped at 5).
6.  **Mandatory Safety Gate (> 15 Subdirectories)**: If BFS discovery finds more than 15 subdirectories, pause immediately and request user approval (via structured single-select question tool if available, or plain chat) before proceeding with full-tree execution or spawning workers.

---

## Workflow

### Step 0: Ecosystem & Verification Discovery

Inspect the repo root manifest to record `VerificationCommand`:
*   Node/TS (`package.json`): `npm test` (or `pnpm test` / `yarn test`)
*   Rust (`Cargo.toml`): `cargo test` | Go (`go.mod`): `go test ./...` | Python (`pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini`/`setup.py`): `pytest`
*   .NET / C# (`*.sln`/`*.slnx`/`*.csproj`): `dotnet test`
*   Make (`Makefile`): `make test` | Bazel (`BUILD`/`BUILD.bazel`): `bazel test //...` | None: `<test-command>`

### Step 1: Startup Branching

If `is_worker` is `true`, jump to **Step 4** for `sub_tree_root`. Otherwise run **Step 2**.

### Step 2: Incremental Scoping & Safety Gate (Root Orchestrator)

1.  **BFS Discovery**: Map `path` level-by-level via a queue (never recursive `find` or `ls -R`). Keep intermediate folders and build manifests (`package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`, `*.sln`, `*.csproj`, `Makefile`, `BUILD`). Ignore symlinks, hidden/system directories (e.g., `.git`, `.antigravity`, `node_modules`, `venv`, `dist`, `build`, `third_party`), and patterns in `.gitignore` / `.egmignore`.
2.  **Safety Gate & Spawning Approval (> 15)**: When running directory count exceeds **15**, pause and ask via single-select gate (`is_multi_select: false`):
    *   `question`: `"The target directory tree contains more than 15 subdirectories. This is a large execution scope: up to 5 parallel workers, and at least one scout per code directory (one per ~1,500 lines of source). Do you want to proceed with full-tree bootstrapping?"`
    *   `options`: `["Yes, proceed with full tree bootstrapping", "No, abort execution"]`
    Wait for the user; abort immediately if declined.
3.  **Bottom-Up Post-Pruning**:
    *   *Recognized Source / Schema Extensions*: Systems (`.c`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.h`, `.hh`, `.hpp`, `.rs`, `.go`, `.zig`, `.lean`, `.f`, `.f90`, `.f95`, `.f03`, `.f08`, `.hs`), Managed (`.java`, `.kt`, `.scala`, `.cs`, `.razor`, `.cshtml`, `.fs`, `.vb`), Scripting (`.py`, `.rb`, `.php`, `.lua`, `.sh`, `.bash`, `.ps1`, `.psm1`, `.psd1`, `.r`, `.R`, `.ex`, `.exs`), Web/Mobile (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.swift`, `.m`, `.dart`), Schemas/IDLs (`.sql`, `.proto`, `.graphql`, `.gql`, `.thrift`, `.prisma`), Infra (`.tf`, `.hcl`, `.cue`). Exclude manifests, lockfiles, fixtures, docs, and `.csv`/`.tsv`/`.parquet`.
    *   *Exclude Test-Only Dirs*: Skip `tests`, `testing`, `testdata`, or dirs holding only `*_test.*`, `*Test.*`, `test_*.*`, `*.spec.*`.
    *   *Non-Code Filtering*: Drop directories with neither direct code nor code-containing subdirectories; keep empty intermediate folders only when descendants hold code.
4.  Compute pruned directory count and max depth, then run **Step 3**.

### Step 3: Execution Strategy Selection (Root Orchestrator)

1.  **Direct (`<= 5` pruned dirs)**: Run **Step 4** inline on `path`, then **Step 5**.
2.  **Parallel Subagent Swarm Strategy (`> 5` pruned dirs)**: Verify `> 15` approval first if applicable. Partition via **Adaptive Depth Partitioning**:
    *   Start at `depth = 1`. Collect nodes at `depth`. If 3-5 nodes, use them as partition roots.
    *   If `< 3`, increment `depth` (max 3) and re-check. If `> 5`, take the 3-4 largest branches separately and combine smaller ones into one fallback subtree.
    *   If `depth == 3` and still `< 3`, pick immediate children of root (or run sequentially).
    *   **Worker Cap**: For each partition subtree root, spawn their Sub-Orchestrators in parallel, never more than 5. Use `egm-bootstrap-orchestrator` (`agents/bootstrap_orchestrator.md`, passing its absolute path if resolved from `<plugin-root>`, or a general-purpose subagent):
        `Prompt`: `"Run egm-bootstrap with path=[path], is_worker=true, sub_tree_root=[partition_root], target_filename=[target_filename]."`
    *   Wait for all worker JSON `subtree_index` payloads, then proceed to **Step 5**.

### Step 4: Sub-Orchestrator Worker Flow

1.  **Scout Setup (`goldfish-explorer`)**: Register (where runtime subagent definition is supported) or prompt a read-only scout (`enable_write_tools: false`, `enable_subagent_tools: false`) with:
    > You are a read-only codebase explorer. Analyze source files in the target directory and return a JSON object matching `{"interface": string[], "invariants": string[], "side_effects": string[]}`. Do not write files. Never infer RPC methods, routes, status enums, or invariants from file or directory names alone; cite exact `[file:symbol_or_flag]` for every entry, and output `["None"]` if no explicit invariants or side effects exist in code.
2.  **Post-Order Traversal (Deepest Leaves First)** across `D`:
    *   **Correction Policy**: If `target_filename` already exists in `D`, read it (never blindly overwrite), scan code via `goldfish-explorer`, extract legacy public symbols, invariants, and side effects as JSON (`{"interface": string[], "invariants": string[], "side_effects": string[]}`), merge with code-verified scout output, and edit `target_filename` preserving valid developer notes.
    *   **Scout Reading & Chunking**: No per-directory or per-file byte cap. List top-level definitions with your search tool first, then read every non-test file in full in chunks of ~**1,500 lines** cut at top-level definitions (never mid-body; small files share a chunk). Spawn one `goldfish-explorer` per chunk in parallel, at most 5 at a time (queue the rest), give each chunk the file's imports and top-level definitions to judge visibility, and merge their JSON. Verify build-manifest deps and `import` / `#include` before attributing RPCs, schemas, or message types locally. Read order: (1) contracts, schemas, build manifests (`.h`, `.hh`, `.hpp`, `.proto`, `.graphql`, `.gql`, `.thrift`, `.prisma`, `.sql` DDL, interfaces; extract exact DDL tables and exported targets); (2) entry points (`main.*`, `index.*`, `lib.*`, `mod.*`, `__init__.py`, dir-named files) then source/query files alphabetically; (3) templates/configs <= 200 lines each (800 in config-only dirs), excluding `.css`/`.scss`; (4) ignore test files (`*_test.*`, `*Test.*`, `test_*.*`, `*.spec.*`) everywhere. On scout timeout/failure, log a warning and use `["(Details pending/documentation failed)"]`.

# Frame Inventory Design System

A focused product design system extracted from the **Frame Inventory** prototype (an OOH out-of-home media operations tool). Built on top of the Global Design System (Global Next theme — Inter type, blue/cyan palette) and extended with the patterns this product introduced: inventory tables, master-data drawers, audit timelines, and stepper-driven creation flows.

## Sources
- `tokens.css` — full Global Design System tokens (Inter font, color palettes, semantic roles, spacing, elevation).
- `styles.css` — component styles built on top of the tokens (buttons, chips, tables, fields, surfaces, banners, timeline).
- `shell.jsx` — app chrome: rail nav, topbar, breadcrumbs, brand mark, icon set.
- `master-data.jsx`, `direction-a.jsx`, `direction-b.jsx` — production-shape examples consumed by the design system.

## Index
- `tokens.css` — design tokens (variables only — copy/import directly).
- `styles.css` — component styles built on those tokens.
- `preview/` — design-system preview cards (rendered in the Design System tab).
- `SKILL.md` — Agent Skill manifest for downstream prompting.
- `Frame Inventory.html` — the prototype that anchors the system.

## Content fundamentals
- **Tone**: operational, factual, second-person where action is required ("Add a frame", "Pick from master data"). Never marketing-y, never exclamatory.
- **Casing**: sentence case for everything — buttons (`New frame`, not `New Frame`), headers, table columns. Acronyms keep their caps (`OOH`, `CMS`, `DSP`).
- **Copy density**: short labels, longer help text below in `--text-secondary`. Inline microcopy preferred over modals.
- **No emoji** in product surfaces. Status uses iconographic dots/chips.
- **Numbers** are factual and contextual ("412 m", "10s · 6/min", "FRM-00214"). Use middle-dot `·` as a soft separator.

## Visual foundations
- **Type**: Inter, 13px body default — dense product UI, not document-style. Headings use the same family with weight (500–600) instead of size jumps.
- **Color**: cool blue primary (`--blue-1000` #046AC4) on near-white surfaces (`--gray-50`). Neutrals do the heavy lifting — color is reserved for status (green/red/orange) and primary actions.
- **Surfaces**: white cards on a `--gray-50` canvas, separated by 1px `--border-subtle` borders. **No drop shadows** on resting surfaces — elevation is reserved for popovers and drawers (`--elev-medium`).
- **Radii**: 4px (`--radius`) for inputs/buttons, 8px (`--radius-lg`) for surfaces, 999px for chips/pills.
- **Spacing**: 8px base — `--sp-1` through `--sp-10`. Most gaps are 16–24px (`--sp-2`, `--sp-3`).
- **Hover**: subtle background tint (`--gray-50` → `--blue-50`), no scale.

# Codex integration

## Install and locate the plugin

For the desktop app, install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357). This listing is desktop-only.

For Codex CLI, install the whole plugin, including its personas and standards:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
codex plugin add egm@egm
```

Start a fresh session after installation. Select the installed `egm` skill
from the available skills. Use its discovered absolute `SKILL.md` path;
do not assume a particular cache directory, version, or checkout location.

From `<plugin>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, the plugin root is three parent
directories above the file. Resolve bundled `agents/`, `resources/`, and
`docs/` paths against that root. Resolve `references/` against the active
skill's directory. Resolve user documents and generated artifacts against
the user's working directory. Never substitute similarly named files in the
user's project for bundled personas or standards.

If the user's prompt or agent instructions file (`AGENTS.md`) has a line
`EGM artifact directory: <path>`, write briefs, drafts, and reports to that
folder. Resolve a relative path against the working directory. If a path from
`AGENTS.md` resolves outside the working directory, after following symbolic
links, ask the user to confirm it before creating the folder or writing there.
If they decline or no one can confirm, use the working directory and say why.
Create the folder if it does not exist.

In ChatGPT Work, a skill may be exposed through a cloud resource identifier
while supporting files live in the installed local bundle. Use the installed
path supplied by the skill inventory or installation metadata for those files;
do not construct cloud resource identifiers for arbitrary supporting paths.
If no installed path is available, report the missing capability instead of
guessing a cache location. Read reviewer filenames and frontmatter from the
bundle: a role such as `egm-design` maps to `agents/design_critic.md`, not
`agents/design.md`. Confirm each resolved path before dispatch.

## Fresh-context reviewers

Inspect the available native subagent tool schema. Tool names can be
namespaced and vary by Codex version. When `spawn_agent` exposes
`fork_context`, explicitly set `fork_context: false` for every Goldfish.
When the schema instead exposes `fork_turns`, use `fork_turns: "none"`.
This applies to reviewers launched by a synthesizer too. Use a general-purpose agent
and pass absolute paths to the persona, standards, target document, and
explicitly selected reading list. Do not pass the parent transcript, private
reasoning, or answers the document is supposed to explain.

Require the reviewer to read its persona, target, and every supplied standard
before returning findings. A missing read or inaccessible file is an incomplete
review, not a clean result. Verify native tool results when the host exposes
them; a parent-written completion summary is not equivalent evidence.

Wait for actual reviewer completion before synthesizing findings. Propagate
failures and timeouts; a launched reviewer is not a completed review. If
nesting is unavailable, dispatch reviewers directly from the parent while

parent-only marker and check the actual child result, not the parent's claim.

literal Codex API. Use a structured question tool only when it is available
and permitted in the current mode, mapping to its actual schema. Otherwise
ask one plain-text question and wait for the answer. Preserve the skill's
readiness and section approval gates; tool unavailability is not approval.

# Frame Inventory Design System

A focused product design system extracted from the **Frame Inventory** prototype (an OOH out-of-home media operations tool). Built on top of the Global Design System (Global Next theme — Inter type, blue/cyan palette) and extended with the patterns this product introduced: inventory tables, master-data drawers, audit timelines, and stepper-driven creation flows.

## Sources
- `tokens.css` — full Global Design System tokens (Inter font, color palettes, semantic roles, spacing, elevation).
- `styles.css` — component styles built on top of the tokens (buttons, chips, tables, fields, surfaces, banners, timeline).
- `shell.jsx` — app chrome: rail nav, topbar, breadcrumbs, brand mark, icon set.
- `master-data.jsx`, `direction-a.jsx`, `direction-b.jsx` — production-shape examples consumed by the design system.

## Index
- `tokens.css` — design tokens (variables only — copy/import directly).
- `styles.css` — component styles built on those tokens.
- `preview/` — design-system preview cards (rendered in the Design System tab).
- `SKILL.md` — Agent Skill manifest for downstream prompting.
- `Frame Inventory.html` — the prototype that anchors the system.

## Content fundamentals
- **Tone**: operational, factual, second-person where action is required ("Add a frame", "Pick from master data"). Never marketing-y, never exclamatory.
- **Casing**: sentence case for everything — buttons (`New frame`, not `New Frame`), headers, table columns. Acronyms keep their caps (`OOH`, `CMS`, `DSP`).
- **Copy density**: short labels, longer help text below in `--text-secondary`. Inline microcopy preferred over modals.
- **No emoji** in product surfaces. Status uses iconographic dots/chips.
- **Numbers** are factual and contextual ("412 m", "10s · 6/min", "FRM-00214"). Use middle-dot `·` as a soft separator.

## Visual foundations
- **Type**: Inter, 13px body default — dense product UI, not document-style. Headings use the same family with weight (500–600) instead of size jumps.
- **Color**: cool blue primary (`--blue-1000` #046AC4) on near-white surfaces (`--gray-50`). Neutrals do the heavy lifting — color is reserved for status (green/red/orange) and primary actions.
- **Surfaces**: white cards on a `--gray-50` canvas, separated by 1px `--border-subtle` borders. **No drop shadows** on resting surfaces — elevation is reserved for popovers and drawers (`--elev-medium`).
- **Radii**: 4px (`--radius`) for inputs/buttons, 8px (`--radius-lg`) for surfaces, 999px for chips/pills.
- **Spacing**: 8px base — `--sp-1` through `--sp-10`. Most gaps are 16–24px (`--sp-2`, `--sp-3`).
- **Hover**: subtle background tint (`--gray-50` → `--blue-50`), no scale.
- **Press**: darker shade of the same token, no scale.
- **Borders**: 1px solid `--border-subtle` for surfaces, `--border-default` for inputs.
- **Animation**: practically none — drawers slide in 160ms, banners fade 120ms. Product is utilitarian; movement is reserved for state changes.
- **Imagery**: none in the chrome. The product is text- and data-first.
- **Iconography**: hand-rolled stroke icons at 1.8px stroke (Lucide-style), defined inline in `shell.jsx`. Domain glyphs (Station / Roadside / Airport / Mall / Bus Shelter) live alongside the UI icon set.

Inline SVG icons exported from `shell.jsx::Icon`. Stroke weight 1.8px, round caps/joins, single-color (`currentColor`). Domain icons are 16–24px. The system covers ~30 glyphs: `search`, `plus`, `pencil`, `trash`, `chev`, `chevL`, `filter`, `map`, `list`, `pin`, `history`, `more`, `link`, `warn`, `info`, `check`, `x`, `station`, `road`, `airport`, `mall`, `bus`, `frame`, `dash`, `cog`, `report`, `school`, `globe`, `download`, `upload`.

No emoji, no third-party icon CDN. If new icons are needed, draw new SVGs in the same stroke style.

## Caveats
- The system is **product-scoped** to Frame Inventory — not yet a brand-wide system.
- No marketing surfaces (landing pages, emails) are covered.
- Dark mode is not addressed.
- The "Inter via Google Fonts" fallback is in place but the WOFF2 files in `fonts/` are the source of truth.
